notes: Petit taxis have meters (insist on using them; 20-30 MAD). The Careem app also works, and the medina is walkable. The airport taxi is a fixed 150 MAD, and bus 19 costs 30 MAD.
SUMMER 38-42°C: sightsee from 8 to 11 in the morning and after 18:00, and spend midday at the riad pool or in a hammam. The Atlas and Essaouira are cooler escapes. Check the dates of Ramadan.

Stay in a riad (a courtyard house) inside the medina; a porter for your luggage costs 20 MAD. Haggling rule: pay a third of the first price. Offers of a 'guide' and the 'this road is closed' line are scams.
Tagine 60-100 MAD, Jemaa stall meal 50, mint tea 15, Majorelle 170 (online), hammam 100-400. Tip 10 MAD.
Women will be more comfortable covering shoulders and knees. Mosque interiors are closed to non-Muslims (see Koutoubia from outside).
Turkish citizens can stay 90 days without a visa. Carry cash in MAD (from ATMs); cards are accepted at riads and restaurants.

stops.name: Koutoubia Mosque
stops.tips: A 77 m minaret, twin of Seville's Giralda. See it from outside, stroll the gardens and use it as your compass in the medina.

stops.name: Bahia Palace
stops.tips: A 19th-century vizier's palace with cedar ceilings and courtyards. It is quiet in the first hour.

stops.name: Saadian Tombs
stops.tips: 16th-century mausoleums rediscovered in 1917, with Carrara marble.

stops.name: Souks Marrakech
stops.tips: Labyrinthine markets selling leather (the Bab Debbagh tanneries), lamps and carpets. Offer a third of the first price and decline offers of a guide.

stops.name: Jemaa el-Fnaa Gece
stops.tips: A UNESCO-listed square with 100+ food stalls (harira soup, merguez, snails), storytellers and the Café de France terrace. Snake charmers will ask for money.

backups.name: Le Jardin Secret
backups.tips: A restored riad garden and tower: shade instead of the souks.

backups.name: Nomad Marrakech
backups.tips: Modern Moroccan food on a rooftop at Rahba Kedima. Book ahead.

stops.name: Jardin Majorelle
stops.tips: A cobalt-blue villa and cactus garden once owned by Yves Saint Laurent. Buy tickets online for the 08:00 opening (they sell out). The Berber museum is included.

stops.name: Musée Yves Saint Laurent
stops.tips: The museum next door. Combined tickets are available, and there is a cafeteria.

stops.name: Gueliz Avenue Mohammed V
stops.tips: The French-built new town, with galleries and the 33 Rue Majorelle concept store.

stops.name: Grand Café de la Poste
stops.tips: A 1920s colonial brasserie in Gueliz.

stops.name: Menara Gardens
stops.tips: A 12th-century pool and pavilion. In winter you get views of the snowy Atlas peaks, and it is lovely at sunset.

backups.name: Amal Women's Training Center
backups.tips: A restaurant run by a women's cooperative. Couscous on Fridays.

backups.name: Cyber Park Arsat Moulay Abdeslam
backups.tips: A shady park beside the medina, close by if you skip Menara.

stops.name: Imlil
stops.tips: 1.5 hours by taxi or tour (1,740 m). A Berber village at the foot of Toubkal, with mules and walnut trees.

stops.name: Aroumd Village Walk
stops.tips: A 1-hour climb from Imlil (guide 200 MAD). Terraced gardens and views of Toubkal, with snow in winter.

stops.name: Berber Home Lunch
stops.tips: Tagine and mint tea in a family home, with a terrace.

stops.name: Kasbah du Toubkal
stops.tips: Tea on the terrace of a mountain kasbah, with valley views. Proceeds support charity.

stops.name: Imlil Waterfall
stops.tips: A short walk above the village. Head back at 17:00.

backups.name: Ourika Valley Setti Fatma
backups.tips: An alternative valley: a 7-waterfall hike and riverside tagine. More touristy.

backups.name: Café Aksaoual Imlil
backups.tips: A café on the village square.

stops.name: Ben Youssef Madrasa
stops.tips: A 14th-century madrasa with zellij tilework, a cedar courtyard and 130 student cells. Restored.

stops.name: Maison de la Photographie
stops.tips: Moroccan photographs from 1870 to 1950. Have coffee on the rooftop terrace, with medina views.

stops.name: Le Jardin Marrakech
stops.tips: A restaurant in a green courtyard with tortoises, in Sidi Abdelaziz.

stops.name: Hammam de la Rose
stops.tips: A traditional hammam with black soap, a scrub mitt and an argan massage. Men and women have separate hours.

stops.name: Terrasse des Épices
stops.tips: A rooftop restaurant with sunset views over the medina and tagine.

backups.name: Hammam Mouassine
backups.tips: A local public hammam. It is cheap, so bring your own scrub mitt.

backups.name: Dar Cherifa
backups.tips: A 16th-century riad café and gallery with a literary bent.

stops.name: Skala de la Kasbah
stops.tips: Take the 3-hour Supratours bus (07:00 from Marrakech). Atlantic ramparts and cannons, a Game of Thrones filming location, and seagulls.

stops.name: Essaouira Medina
stops.tips: A white-and-blue UNESCO medina with thuya wood workshops and art galleries.

stops.name: Essaouira Fishing Port
stops.tips: Fresh fish from the blue boats in the port. Haggle by the kilo, and try the sardines.

stops.name: Essaouira Beach
stops.tips: A wide, windy beach with kitesurfing and camel rides. Hendrix legend (Diabat).

stops.name: Taros Café
stops.tips: A rooftop terrace overlooking the port, with gnawa music. Catch the 17:30 bus back.

backups.name: Sidi Kaouki
backups.tips: A surf village beach 25 km away. Go by taxi.

stops.name: Mellah and Lazama Synagogue
stops.tips: The old Jewish quarter, with a spice market (Mellah), a synagogue and the Miara cemetery.

stops.name: Dar Si Said Museum
stops.tips: A museum of Moroccan carpets and woodwork, with the loveliest courtyard.

stops.name: Marché Central Gueliz
stops.tips: A new-town market for fruit and a quick lunch.

stops.name: Agafay Desert
stops.tips: A stony desert 40 minutes from the city. Camel rides, quad bikes, sunset tea and a camp dinner (tour about 400 MAD).

stops.name: Agafay Desert Camp Dinner
stops.tips: Tagine and Berber music at the camp, included in the tour. Stargazing.

backups.name: Palmeraie
backups.tips: A palm grove on the edge of the city, with camel rides. Close by if you skip Agafay.

backups.name: Al Fassia Gueliz
backups.tips: A women-run Moroccan classic. Try the lamb shank.

stops.name: El Badi Palace
stops.tips: The ruins of a 16th-century 'incomparable' palace, with storks and pools. The Koutoubia minbar is displayed here.

stops.name: Place des Ferblantiers
stops.tips: The tinsmiths' square. Buy a lamp as a souvenir, and have a drink on the Kosybar terrace.

stops.name: Bacha Coffee
stops.tips: A coffee salon in a 1910 pasha's palace with 200 coffees. Expect a queue. A fitting farewell.

stops.name: Marrakech Menara Airport
stops.tips: 20 minutes by taxi (fixed 150 MAD). Farewell.

backups.name: Dar el Bacha Museum
backups.tips: The Museum of Confluences. Visit it instead of the coffee.

backups.name: Patisserie des Princes
backups.tips: Moroccan sweets (kaab el ghzal), near Bab Agnaou.
